record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded open convex subset of R^d with Lipschitz boundary and 0 in its interior. For 0 <= beta < d and f : Z^d -> R, define the discrete centered fractional maximal operator associated to Omega by M_{Omega,beta} f(n) = sup_{r>=0} N(0,r)^{beta/d - 1} sum_{m in Omega(0,r)} |f(n+m)|, where N(x,r) counts lattice points in the Omega-ball Omega(x,r). When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), does every discrete function f satisfy ||∇M_{Omega,beta} f||_{ell^q(Z^d)} <= C(d,Omega,beta) ||∇f||_{ell^1(Z^d)}? More generally, does inequality (6.4) hold for all alpha <= beta and q = d/(d-beta+alpha)? The paper asks the analogous questions for the uncentered operator as well.

evidence.quote: Given 0 ≤ β < d and f : Zd → R, we denote by MΩ,β the discrete centered fractional maximal operator associated to Ω, i.e. MΩ,β f (n) = sup_{r≥0} 1/N(0, r)^{1−β/d} ∑_{m∈Ω(0,r)} |f(n + m)|.

Question 11. Let 0 ≤ β < 1 and q = d/(d − β). For a discrete function f : Zd → R do we have ||∇MΩ,β f||_{ℓq(Zd)} ≤ C(d, Ω, β) ||∇f||_{ℓ1(Zd)}? More generally, does the inequality (6.4) hold for all α ≤ β and q = d/(d − β + α)? (Analogous questions for the uncentered operator.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded open convex set with Lipschitz boundary that contains the origin in its interior. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $r\ge 0$ set $\Omega(x,r)=x+r\,\Omega$, and let $N(x,r)=\#(\Omega(x,r)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)$ denote the number of lattice points in $\Omega(x,r)$.

For $0\le \beta<d$ and $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, define the discrete centered fractional maximal operator associated to $\Omega$ by
$$M_{\Omega,\beta} f(n)=\sup_{r\ge 0}\frac{1}{N(0,r)^{1-\beta/d}}\sum_{m\in\Omega(0,r)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d}|f(n+m)|, \qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}^d.$$
Define the uncentered version $\widetilde{M}_{\Omega,\beta}f(n)$ analogously, taking the supremum over all $\Omega$-balls $\Omega(x,r)$ containing $n$.

For $g:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ let $\nabla g$ denote the discrete gradient $(\nabla g)(n)=\bigl(g(n+e_i)-g(n)\bigr)_{i=1}^d$, and for $1\le q<\infty$ write $\|\nabla g\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z}^d)}=\bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}^d}|\nabla g(n)|^q\bigr)^{1/q}$.

(a) Let $0\le\beta<1$ and $q=d/(d-\beta)$. Does there exist a constant $C=C(d,\Omega,\beta)$ such that for every $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$\|\nabla M_{\Omega,\beta}f\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\le C\,\|\nabla f\|_{\ell^1(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\,?$$

(b) More generally, given $0\le\alpha\le\beta<1$ and $q=d/(d-\beta+\alpha)$, does the inequality
$$\|\nabla M_{\Omega,\beta}f\|_{\ell^q(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\le C(d,\Omega,\beta,\alpha)\,\|\nabla f\|_{\ell^{d/(d-\alpha)}(\mathbb{Z}^d)}$$
hold for all $f:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{R}$?

(c) Do the analogous inequalities hold with $M_{\Omega,\beta}$ replaced by the uncentered operator $\widetilde{M}_{\Omega,\beta}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Endpoint Sobolev bounds for fractional maximal operators in the continuous setting were established by Beltran–Madrid (arXiv:2010.05561, Math. Z. 2022). For the discrete setting on general convex Ω-balls in Z^d as posed here, no resolution appears in the literature; partial results exist only for specific cases (e.g., ℓ¹-balls and multisublinear variants). The problem as stated for general convex Ω with Lipschitz boundary appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev Bounds for Fractional Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Both centered and uncentered Hardy-Littlewood fractional maximal operators are weakly differentiable... covers the endpoint case p=1 for 0 < α < 1.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous-setting endpoint problem solved by Beltran-Madrid; discrete analogue on general convex Ω not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint regularity of discrete multisublinear fractional maximal operators associated with ℓ1-balls
status_evidence.snippet: Discrete m-sublinear fractional maximal operators associated with ℓ¹-balls, centered and uncentered versions, mapping into BV(Z^d).
status_evidence.claim: Only specific (ℓ¹-ball, multisublinear) discrete cases are treated; general convex case open.
